## Appearance

Matthew Cuthbert is an odd-looking man with an ungainly figure and stooping shoulders. He has long, iron-gray hair that reaches down to his shoulders. Additionally, he sports a full, soft brown beard that he has maintained continuously since he was twenty years old.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003)_

## Personality

Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally shy, quiet, and reticent man who naturally prefers silence over conversation and is uncommunicative when confronted with arguments. He harbors a deep fear of women, excepting only [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and Mrs. Rachel, as he uncomfortably suspects they are secretly laughing at him, and he possesses a mortal dread of little girls. Known to be the shyest man alive, he hates being among strangers, dislikes seeking excitement, and is frightened at the prospect of meeting new people. Despite his overwhelming bashfulness, he is a deeply patient, wise, good-natured, and loving person who acts as a remarkably sympathetic listener. He is extremely hardworking, yet remarkably persistent and stubborn, silently holding fast to his opinions and whims once he forms them.

## History

Matthew Cuthbert, who had worn a full brown beard since the age of twenty and had never gone courting, lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with his sister [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md). When he traveled to [Bright River](../codex/places.md#bright-river) station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he instead discovered a young orphan girl named [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md). Refusing to leave her behind, he brought her home and quietly advocated for keeping her despite Marilla's initial reluctance. He later secretly visited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) during a punishment to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), and he frequently showed his support for her, such as bringing her chocolates and warm encouragement. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) was saving up to buy a flag at school, Matthew went behind Marilla's back to enlist Mrs. Lynde's help in getting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas).

As [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) grew older, Matthew willingly agreed to pay for her extra studies in the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) class so she could train to become a teacher. Despite facing failing health, he took great pride in Anne's academic triumphs, including her tying for first place on the entrance exams and later winning the Avery scholarship at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy). During Anne's return home to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), Matthew spent a peaceful day walking with her and tenderly expressed how proud he was of her. Shortly afterward, Matthew suffered a fatal collapse and died suddenly after reading a newspaper report detailing the failure of the Abbey Bank.

## Quotes

> "Well, she didn’t. She brought her. I asked the stationmaster. And I had to bring her home. She couldn’t be left there, no matter where the mistake had come in."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P5](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0005)

> “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P25](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0025)

> “Well now, I guess you’ll manage all right,” said Matthew, looking at Anne’s white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes. “You just go right to bed and have a good sleep. I’ll do all the chores.”
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P38](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0038)

> "and—and—I dunno—but I’d like—I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be. If it wouldn’t be asking too much I—I’d like them made in the new way."
>
> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P26](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0026)

> “Well now, I was proud of her and I did tell her so ‘fore she went upstairs,” said Matthew. “We must see what we can do for her some of these days, Marilla. I guess she’ll need something more than Avonlea school by and by.”

> — Matthew Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P60](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0060)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--matthew-cuthbert.md)

Matthew forms an immediate, quiet bond with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) after accidentally bringing her to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) instead of the orphan boy he and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) intended to adopt. He acts as her gentle advocate, secretly persuading [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) to keep her and encouraging [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to apologize to Mrs. [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) after a conflict. Matthew frequently supports [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) through small acts of kindness, such as bringing her chocolates, establishing a warm and lasting friendship with her.

- Friend of — best of friends  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXIV. Miss Stacy and Her Pupils Get Up a Concert P17](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0017), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P8](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0008)</sub>
